title: `toolRoot()` survived bundling, and the reader still passes roots explicitly
statement: Under `next build` + `next start` with Next.js 16.3.2 and Turbopack, `toolRoot()` — which resolves from `import.meta.url` inside `lib/content-root.mjs` — returned the repository root correctly from within the built server, matching `process.cwd()`. Next.js traced `lib/` rather than inlining it.
notes: ⚠️ RECORDED BECAUSE THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG. The reader was designed around an expectation that bundling would repoint `import.meta.url` at a build artefact and silently break every default derived from `toolRoot()`. Measured: it did not. The comment asserting otherwise was corrected rather than left standing. ⚠️ THE DESIGN DID NOT CHANGE, and the reason is worth separating from the prediction. Whether `import.meta.url` survives is a property of the bundler's choices — a standalone output, a different builder, or a future Turbopack decision could inline `lib/`, and the failure would be a real directory that is not the project. Passing `process.cwd()` explicitly costs nothing and does not depend on a behaviour this project does not control. ⚠️ `loadBearing: false`: nothing rests on this holding. It is recorded so the next person does not re-derive the same wrong expectation from the same reasoning.
